chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbbād ibn Ṣuhayb, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a Christian who slandered a Muslim and said to him, “O fornicator,”

So he عليه السلام said: “He is to be flogged with eighty lashes for the right of the Muslim, and eighty lashes minus one for the sanctity of Islam; his head is to be shaved, and he is to be paraded among the people of his religion so that others besides him may be deterred.”

key_terms.قَذَفَ: falsely accused with a charge of sexual immorality
key_terms.لِحَقِّ الْمُسْلِمِ: for the violated right of the Muslim person
key_terms.لِحُرْمَةِ الْإِسْلَامِ: for the violated sanctity of Islam
key_terms.نَصْرَانِيٍّ: a Christian subject of the ruling in this report
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ: he is to be flogged as a legal punishment
key_terms.يُحْلَقُ رَأْسُهُ: his head is to be shaved
key_terms.يُنَكَّلَ: to serve as a deterrent or exemplary punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a Christian falsely accuses a Muslim of zina in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a Christian who falsely accuses a Muslim of zina. It specifies corporal punishment for violating the Muslim’s right and the sanctity of Islam, along with a public disciplinary measure intended to deter others.
